description:
FILED s540b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-13), docs/speed-low-hanging-review-s540.md THE LIST.  Code sha 05806e16.

WHERE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp `p-hash` (~line 16477): `(loop for item in (%p-tie-views pairs) ... append ... collect ...)` copies every pair into `flat`, then `(make-hash-table :test 'equal)` -- SBCL's default size is 7, so any literal with 8+ keys (objects: `bless { ... }` with many fields, JSON-like records, Pod::Simple nodes) grows the table once or twice (sb-impl::grow-hash-table was 5 % of the podtext profile).

MEASUREMENT (scratch/s540b/lev/hash-presize.lisp redefines p-hash: when no pair item is a vector or a hash table, size the table to (ceiling n 2) and insert straight from the argument list; otherwise the old body; ab.pl --lever, best of 5, legs/leg2.log, load 1.3):
  anonhash (300 k x a 10-key `{ id => $i, name => "n$i", a => 1, ... }`)  0.267 -> 0.226 s  -15.4 %  (C/A +0.4 %)
  moo-objs                                                              +1.8 %  (C/A +0.8 %: not measurable)
  podtext                                                                -0.0 %  (its growth is in element stores, not in p-hash)

THE FIX: in p-hash, the no-flatten fast path with :size; the same presize in the flatten path (the count is known after flattening).  Optional sibling: p-array-init's growth from 0.  Runtime only.

BAR: hash rows of the gate (grep -l 'p-hash' Pl/t), sweep (hash.t, hashassign.t +0), tied-hash guard rows (%p-tie-views must still see a tied operand), the anonhash row reproduced, everyday.

DO NOT: presize from the ARGUMENT count when an item is a hash or a vector (it flattens to more pairs); do not skip %p-tie-views.

=== s540 (2026-11-13) === scheduled: s540/s540d-prompt.md (the USER: the speed fixing is a normal task).


=== DONE (s540d) ===
BUILT (runtime only).  p-hash reads a pair list with no hash or array to spread IN PLACE (%p-hash-from-pairs; a list that spreads is flattened first, as before; %p-tie-views still sees a tied operand) and, ABOVE 7 pairs, makes its EQUAL table for the pair count; up to 7 pairs it keeps SBCL's DEFAULT table.  That split is a fix-forward (the s540d commit "#4984 fix-forward", s542): the first version passed a computed :size for every constructor, and the full bench read the one-pair `bless { v => $_[1] }, $_[0]` rows (blessnew / blessnew-d / blessdes) 10-12 % slower than the base, twice (K=5, then K=9 against a base-vs-base band <= 2.2 %).  Cause, measured in-process: the constant-argument `(make-hash-table :test 'equal)` compiles to SB-IMPL::MAKE-HASH-TABLE-USING-DEFAULTS, a computed :size to the keyword MAKE-HASH-TABLE: 0.143 vs 0.176 s per million (~33 ns a hash); SBCL's default holds 7 keys (the 8th grows it to 10), so nothing small is lost.  MEASURED (quiet, best of 5 / 7 whole runs, base 24988e35 vs the tree): Final (against 75904a35 = main with s540c, legs/bench4.log + bench5.log, quiet): whole runs best of 7: the 10-key `{...}` loop 0.271 -> 0.233 s (-14.0 %, band 0.5), the one-pair `bless` loop 0.503 -> 0.500 s (-0.8 %, band 0.8), moo-objs 0.0 % (band 1.5); bench-exec K=9: blessnew -1.5 % (band -0.5), arrhash +0.9, hashcopy +1.5, moo-objs +2.8 (all inside or above their bands); the DESTROY-registry rows blessnew-d / blessdes still -7.3 / -6.8 % (band <= 0.2): not attributed (the tree conses less on them, GC time the same) -- filed #5024.  (bench1, before the fix-forward, against 24988e35: 10-key loop 0.272 -> 0.234 s, -13.8 %).  Guards: Pl/t/perf-levers-16.t row 3 (a 20-pair constructor's table = one made for 20; the base grows to 28) + row 8 (perl's output: spread hash + array, a later key wins, empty, 20 pairs, nested).  The small-constructor path has no mechanism row (the two tables are identical objects; only SBCL's construction path differs): its guard is bench-exec's blessnew rows.  Sweep hash.t / hashassign.t = baseline; companion op/hash.t 467/27, op/hashassign.t 305/4 = the snapshot (re-run on the final runtime, legs/comp2.log).
subject: PERF (s540b, measured): the anonymous-hash constructor p-hash conses a full copy of its pair list and grows an unsized EQUAL table -- presizing + skipping the copy when nothing needs flattening is -15 % on a 10-key `{...}` constructor loop
